headline: Facing a projected deficit, Southborough initiated FY28 override planning, narrowed Neary renovation plans, and allowed retail cannabis delivery to proceed.
synopsis: Faced with an anticipated FY28 budget deficit exceeding $2 million, the Select Board and Advisory Committee instructed departments to prepare dual budget submissions showing level service alongside no-increase budgets. To curb municipal costs, the Select Board voted to enter expedited negotiations over employee health insurance plan designs under state law. The Elementary School Building Committee refined renovation options for Neary Elementary School, removing district administrative offices from future designs ahead of an expected March 2027 Town Meeting vote. Town officials also confirmed an October 17, 2026 Special Town Meeting, with warrant articles set to address appointed town clerk governance, two-family zoning rules, and revised Community Preservation Act requests. Meanwhile, the Select Board voted against opting out of state cannabis delivery rules, permitting licensed retailers to deliver directly to Southborough residents.

top_items.title: Dual-budget directive issued amid projected FY28 operating deficit
top_items.why: Officials project a municipal budget shortfall exceeding $2 million to maintain current services. Departments must submit both level-service requests and frozen budgets illustrating necessary service cuts.
top_items.body: The Select Board and Advisory Committee met jointly to address FY28 operating budget challenges, entering the fiscal planning cycle with about $700,000 in excess levy capacity against an anticipated deficit of over $2 million. Board members directed department heads to prepare two budget scenarios: Budget A, preserving level service with salaries and holding non-salary expenses to FY26 actuals; and Budget B, showing zero dollar increase over FY27. The exercises will determine what service reductions would be required if the town decides against presenting an operating override to voters.

top_items.title: Neary School project eliminates central offices and phased repair plan
top_items.why: The Elementary School Building Committee dropped school district administrative offices from Neary Elementary renovation designs and rejected a 10-year capital maintenance schedule.
top_items.body: Tappé Architects presented addition and renovation concepts for Neary Elementary School, including an Option 4 design featuring a 13,000-square-foot standalone gymnasium, stage, and expanded front entryway. Following committee debate, members instructed the architectural team to exclude the central school district administration offices from future building designs. The committee also formally rejected a proposed 10-year phased capital maintenance schedule spanning 2028 through 2037, concluding that a decade of continuous construction would excessively disrupt elementary students.

top_items.title: Select Board accepts state statute to renegotiate municipal health plans
top_items.why: The board voted 5-0 to accept MGL Chapter 32B, Sections 21-23 to pursue expedited health insurance plan design modifications with the Public Employee Committee.
top_items.body: Seeking to manage healthcare costs that account for 11.2 percent of Southborough's municipal budget, the Select Board voted unanimously to adopt statutory procedures under Chapter 32B. The action enables expedited negotiations with employee bargaining representatives over plan design alterations intended to reduce premium expenses beginning July 1, 2027. Neighboring Northborough and the regional school district adopted the same statutory mechanism during the same week, setting up coordinated negotiations across all three local governmental entities.

top_items.title: Select Board allows retail marijuana home delivery in Southborough
top_items.why: A motion to seek a municipal opt-out waiver from state cannabis delivery rules failed 1-4, allowing licensed couriers to deliver adult-use cannabis to residents.
top_items.body: The Select Board evaluated whether Southborough should exercise a two-year municipal opt-out waiver permitted under Massachusetts regulations to prohibit licensed commercial marijuana delivery to local households. Board members noted that only 13 of 154 eligible communities statewide had chosen to opt out. A motion to enact the local delivery opt-out was defeated by a 1-4 vote, confirming that state-licensed couriers may deliver retail cannabis products directly to adult residents aged 21 and older.

top_items.title: CPA funding requests updated for golf course irrigation and Peninsula Trail
top_items.why: The Community Preservation Committee reviewed increased funding requests for the golf course and a scaled-back Peninsula Trail footbridge ahead of Special Town Meeting.
top_items.body: The Golf Course Committee and Department of Public Works presented an updated golf course irrigation budget of $1,087,296, reflecting a 15 percent construction contingency and requesting $433,546 in additional CPA money alongside $100,000 from the Golf Revolving Fund. Meanwhile, the Trails Committee adjusted its application for the Peninsula Trail connection to $466,628, removing the boardwalk component to construct only a prefabricated footbridge and requesting $210,796 in new CPA funds while repurposing prior Town Meeting balances. The Recreation Commission announced it would withdraw its Fayville Memorial Park application to resolve parking design questions and await federal grant decisions.

top_items.title: Municipal Technology Committee conditionally backs Police drone acquisition
top_items.why: The committee voted 4-0 to recommend approval for the Police Department's drone purchase, subject to privacy restrictions and staged program reviews.
top_items.body: Police Chief Ryan Newell presented a five-year deployment plan for a Skydio X10 public safety drone integrated with the department's Axon Evidence system. Addressing potential resident privacy and operational concerns, the Municipal Technology Committee endorsed the acquisition under a phased deployment structure. The conditional recommendation requires pre-deployment system verification, an initial restricted pilot phase, and formal operational reviews after 90 days and 12 months.

top_items.title: Boards review zoning change to allow immediate two-family conversions
top_items.why: Proposed bylaw amendments would eliminate a rule requiring a single-family home to exist for at least two years before converting into a two-family dwelling.
top_items.body: Both the Zoning Board of Appeals and the Planning Board reviewed proposed amendments to Southborough's zoning bylaw concerning two-family dwellings ahead of Town Meeting. The proposal removes the two-year existence prerequisite for conversions, updates duplex and townhouse definitions, and retains special permit requirements across all districts. Discussions focused on distinguishing two-family dwellings from accessory dwelling units, assessing lot coverage standards, and evaluating impacts across residential and industrial zones.
